title: CallLint compiler job
description: One unit of pending compiler work (calllint.compiler-job.v1; §7.1, §10.2, ADR 0061). The queue is IDEMPOTENT by identity, not by attempt: `inputDigest` plus `jobType` plus `subjectKey` is the canonical DDL's UNIQUE triple, so re-enqueueing unchanged inputs updates the existing row instead of growing the queue — a rolling compiler that re-reads a source every hour must not accumulate one job per read. `state` is fail-closed: `FAILED` and `DEAD_LETTER` are TERMINAL and never re-run implicitly, because a job that silently retries forever is how a compiler burns a rate limit and reports nothing. `leaseOwner`/`leaseExpiresAt` are nullable together and only populated while `LEASED`: a lease is a claim with an expiry, so a worker that dies leaves an expired lease another worker may reclaim, rather than a permanently-held row. `lastErrorDigest` points into the CAS instead of inlining the error, keeping the queue row small and the error bytes content-addressed. `availableAt` is an injected ISO-8601 timestamp — the backoff schedule is computed by the caller, never from a wall-clock read inside the compile path (INV-R6, §9.5). Written by R-6; the table and schema land in R-1 with the rest of the canonical DDL.
